success_patterns: Slot type was matched to the clue's category noun: 'this film' gave the film title (Thunder Road) rather than its theme song, and 'god' gave a single deity name.
The agent used the qualifier in the clue ('Greek', 'erotic') to pick between near-synonyms (Eros over Cupid), which Rule 2 already covers.

For a fill-in clue ('became the Duchess of it'), the agent returned only the missing word (York), without 'Duchess of' or 'Duke and Duchess of York'. Rule 4's 'give only the MISSING part' already covers this.

The answer was an entity repeated across many passages together with the clue's anchor details. One passage repeated the clue with no answer after it, and the agent ignored it and took the well-supported entity from topical passages.
All three answers were short bare names in the answer tags, with no descriptors, and all passed on the first step.

patch.reasoning: Every observed success follows behaviors the skill already encodes: type matching (Rule 2), qualifier honoring (Rule 2), missing-part-only answers (Rule 4), and picking the entity that recurs across passages with the clue's anchors (Rule 3). The skill is already long and the optimizer memory says to consolidate rather than stack bullets, so adding more text would risk overfitting and conflicts. The right move is a no-op.
